newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar closes higher after c. bank move.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar closes higher after c. bank move.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar ended firmer against its U.S. counterpart on Monday after the central bank's Saturday intervention to help the local currency rebound from its week of tumbles, dealers said.
The local unit finished at T$28.654 against Saturday's T$28.705 finish.
Turnover through dealers was heavy at US$372 million.
The local currency firmed in early Monday trade after the central bank made clear on Saturday that it would not let the Taiwan dollar continue to tumble, dealers said.
"The central bank has set the rules for the market. Despite persistent greenback demand, the market is very careful not to upset the central bank," said one dealer.

The Taiwan dollar rate fell to an intra-day low of T$28.730 in the afternoon due to renewed U.S. dollar buying, but dealers said a late inflow of foreign equity funds pushed the Taiwan dollar to a higher end.

The Taiwan dollar, which faced intense U.S. dollar buying pressure, tumbled more than four percent last week, prompting the central bank to raise two key interest rates on Thursday in a bid to maintain forex market stability.
A range of T$28.60-80 was seen for Tuesday.
